requirements.requirement: Repair supervisor.py so it starts exactly the requested number of short jobs, remains running until they finish, and reaps every child.
requirements.summary: Runs with six jobs before restart and five jobs after restart directly showed the running supervisor with exactly the requested number of children. Each supervisor then exited successfully, with no remaining child or zombie processes.

requirements.requirement: Record every job in results.tsv with exit status 0 for even-numbered jobs and 3 for odd-numbered jobs, while preserving all previous results.
requirements.summary: The original header and previous record remained an unchanged prefix. Six validated records were appended before restart and five after restart, with exactly one record per requested job and the required parity-based statuses. Final validation covered the complete file.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The solution uses the installed Python 3.12 standard library and made no package changes. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were identical before and after the repair and restart; package-health observations remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, the restart was scheduled and observed through connection loss, the post-restart boot identity differed, and services, files, preserved data, and the repaired workflow recovered successfully. The fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1
